2608.05628.title: SkillHEX: Improving Agent Skills via Hypothesis-Driven Autonomous Exploration and Exploitation
2608.05628.paper_summary: Although agent skills equip LLMs with reusable procedural knowledge, manual maintenance suffers from high costs, unscalability, and misalignment. Real-world deployments thus require autonomous, on-demand skill evolution at test time, constrained by limited interaction budgets and a lack of training or validation sets. This setting introduces a severe sparse reward challenge, where outcomes conflate multiple latent failure causes. Under such ambiguity, existing methods that greedily refine a single incumbent skill are particularly vulnerable to an exploitation trap, allowing early misdiagnoses to exhaust limited trials along unproductive trajectories. To address this, we introduce SkillHEX, a closed-loop framework coupling hypothesis-driven self-verification with evidence-guided tree search. SkillHEX translates falsifiable failure hypotheses into executable tests, producing diagnostic evidence as dense reward without additional environment attempts. This evidence guides a search over persistent skill-revision branches, dynamically balancing the exploitation of supported edits with the exploration of plausible alternatives. Evaluated on 87 tasks from SkillsBench, SkillHEX outperforms existing self-evolving methods and achieves an average pass rate of 55.9% and 57.9% using GPT-5.3-Codex and Claude Opus 4.7 under a five-iteration budget, respectively.
2608.05628.paper_summary_zh: 雖然代理技能使大型語言模型具備可重複使用的程序知識，但手動維護面臨高成本、無法擴展和不一致的問題。因此，現實世界的部署需要在測試時進行自主的、按需的技能演變，這受到有限互動預算和缺乏訓練或驗證集的限制。這種情況引入了嚴重的稀疏獎勵挑戰，其中結果混合了多個潛在的失敗原因。在這種模糊性下，現有方法貪婪地細化單一現有技能，特別容易陷入利用陷阱，使早期的誤診耗盡有限的嘗試，沿著無效的軌跡前進。為了解決這個問題，我們引入了SkillHEX，一個將假設驅動的自我驗證與證據引導的樹搜索相結合的閉環框架。SkillHEX將可證偽的失敗假設轉化為可執行的測試，產生診斷證據作為密集獎勵，而無需額外的環境嘗試。這些證據指導對持久技能修訂分支的搜索，動態平衡支持編輯的利用與可行替代方案的探索。在87個來自SkillsBench的任務上進行評估時，SkillHEX的表現超過現有的自我演變方法，並在五次迭代預算下，分別使用GPT-5.3-Codex和Claude Opus 4.7達到平均通過率55.9%和57.9%。
